$comment: PRODUCT READINESS, and how every figure in it is derived (PW phase, round 80).
THIS IS NOT THE ENGINEERING COMPLETION FIGURE AND MUST NEVER BE COMPARED TO IT.
coordination/PROJECT_STATUS.md reports DONE/total over control/tasks.json; that
answers 'has the board been worked'. This file answers a different question --
'can a person install this on a Windows PC and watch something' -- and the two
were 62/64 and roughly one third of the way there on the same tree, which is
exactly why they are separate files.
DERIVATION, stated so it cannot quietly become a task count. Each dimension
lists CAPABILITIES a user would notice. Each capability is scored:
present = 1.0   implemented AND reachable by a user of the shipped app
partial = 0.5   implemented behind a seam a user cannot reach, or
implemented for one target/case but not the shipped one
absent  = 0.0   no implementation
A dimension's figure is the sum of its item scores over its item count.
Overall is the WEIGHTED mean of the dimensions, using the weights below --
not a mean of means, because the dimensions are not equally load-bearing for
'can a person watch something'.
WHY 'partial' EXISTS AND IS NOT A HEDGE. Three capabilities in this product --
profiles, watchlist, progress -- have complete, tested, reviewed HTTP APIs and
no user interface whatsoever. Scoring them absent would erase real reviewed
work; scoring them present would claim a person can use them. 0.5 is the only
honest answer and the evidence field says which half exists.
EVERY item's `evidence` is a repository path or an explicit statement of
absence. An item with no evidence is a defect in this file.
=== ROUND 107 RE-SCORE: READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING THE FIGURE TO AN EARLIER ONE ===
Overall moved from 46% to 60%, and ALMOST NONE OF THAT IS WORK DONE IN ROUND 107.
It is this file catching up with work that had already landed, in some cases
many rounds earlier. A figure that rises because the product improved and a
figure that rises because the instrument was wrong are different events, and
treating the 14 points as progress would be the exact mistake this file's own
header warns about for the task count.
Nine items stated as FACT things that had stopped being true, several citing
line numbers and absences as evidence. The worst: packagingRelease reported 0%
and said 'Every CI job is ubuntu-latest; no windows-latest runner exists' on a
tree where CI builds, digests, installs, verifies and uninstalls a real Windows
installer on every push. Also stale: the installer, the app identity, the Tauri
shell, capability routing, track selection, offline/network state, Windows test
execution, and several notes describing PW-0102, PW-0303, PW-0312 and PW-0403
as in review when all four are DONE.
EVERY NOTE NOW SAYS WHICH KIND OF CHANGE IT RECORDS, in its first words:
CORRECTED  -- the instrument was wrong; the product did not change.
CHANGED    -- the product moved.
CORRECTED AND CHANGED -- the note was stale AND work landed.
Keep that convention. It is what makes the next reading trustworthy.
THE SCORING RULES WERE APPLIED, NOT RELAXED. 'present' still means reachable by
a user. So the Windows installer is present and the Tauri shell is PARTIAL,
because an installer that CI produces and nobody has launched is not a running
application; the player adapter, capability routing and track selection are all
partial because player-surface.tsx still drives the controller directly and
nothing routes through the boundary. Four items went UP by half a point only.
WHAT THE CORRECTED FIGURE MAKES VISIBLE, which the wrong one hid: the dimensions
that are genuinely stuck are realContent at 10% -- blocked on a licensed
provider, which is the commander's -- and nativePlayback at 55%, blocked behind
PW-0103 on the commander's Windows hardware. They were previously obscured by
dimensions that only looked stuck.
The rules, the weights and the dimension list were NOT touched. PL-0716.
Weighted because the dimensions are not equally load-bearing for a usable
Windows product. nativePlayback and windowsDesktop are weighted highest
because without them there is no Windows application at all, whatever the
rest scores. engineeringFoundation is weighted LOW despite being nearly
complete, for the same reason: it is necessary and it is not sufficient,
and weighting it high would let a finished foundation flatter the figure.

CORRECTED round 107 (the instrument was wrong, the product did not change): "No rate limit on any route" is false for the AUTH routes and true for the application's own. better-auth 1.7.5 enables rate limiting whenever the server is in production -- `enabled: options.rateLimit?.enabled ?? isProduction` -- with a 100-per-60-seconds default and a special rule of THREE PER TEN SECONDS on anything under /sign-in or /sign-up, keyed per client IP and path. Nobody configured that; it is the library's default and packages/auth passes no rateLimit option at all. Partial rather than present for exactly that reason: an unexamined default is not a policy, it applies to no route this product wrote, and PL-0715 is very likely a consequence of the half that exists
